# ↪️ Pull Request

<!---
Provide a general summary of the pull request here
Please look for any issues that this PR resolves and tag them in the PR.
-->
Uses the Vue v3 `@vue/compiler-sfc` API.
Closes #3364
Closes #1333
Fixes #2721
Fixes #1183
Heavily inspired by [DarioDaF](https://github.com/parcel-bundler/parcel/issues/3364#issuecomment-598786210)'s transformer.

WORKING:
- Core functionality
- Any template/scripting/styling languages
- Scoped CSS
- Requiring other SFCs
- Autoinstalling missing template/scripting/styling packages
- CSS Modules (including custom names)
- Custom blocks

BUGS:
- SFC is parsed multiple times because Parcel considers different pipelines to be totally separate (`canReuseAST` is never called as a result)

UNTESTED:
- HMR (likely working but not sure how to test it vs. standard HMR)
- `vue-router`, `vuex`, etc. (though these should work just fine since they're merely JavaScript)

## 💻 Examples

<!-- Examples help us understand the requested feature better -->
See `vue` integration tests


## ✔️ PR Todo

- [x] Added/updated unit tests for this change
- [x] Included links to related issues/PRs

@mischnic I wrote a quick integration test `vue-full`, and it has started breaking in the rewrite with named pipelines because for some reason, the assets imported from the JS code generated by the transformer aren't added to the asset graph. Could you take a look?

EDIT: I've since fixed the issue. I hadn't used `uniqueKey` to distinguish the JS files.

Opening for review because the transformer supports most operations. I still need to fix the tests and the multiple-parsing of each SFC, but I could definitely use some suggestions on both of those fronts. I don't know of any way to avoid reparsing the SFC, and I'm not sure how to test this because unlike before, `run(bundleGraph)` won't work because Vue references browser globals.

<strike>@DeMoorJasper Somehow, allowing `.vue` extensions to [resolve without an extension](https://github.com/parcel-bundler/parcel/pull/4892/commits/e4ebfc8f96f005d4a9d96c5e911b5b79be03caac#diff-55ff0e36af2108f79d8af002e7dc6841R29) is the bug that caused HMR to fail on macOS. I think you might want to take a look into the Parcel core because that seems like (very) unintended behavior.</strike>

EDIT: Apparently that was a one-time bug. It seems to be working again now.
